experience: Choose a side and watch the sentence disappear toward the other cursor. The empty result looks identical; the paths that made it do not.
mechanism: Backspace consumes characters to the left of its cursor. Delete consumes characters to the right. Both leave the same blank line, with the erased characters briefly visible as a fading trail.
mechanisms: Two cursors consume one fixed line from opposite ends
A fading trail briefly records the characters each cursor erased
observation: A text cursor has two familiar ways to erase: Backspace removes what is behind it; Delete removes what is ahead. The word “delete” hides a directional choice.
premise: One line of text sits between two cursor marks. Each cursor removes one character at a time, advancing from its own side until the line is gone.
scope: A single-screen 2D interactive typographic study, completable today.
specificity: The work turns the paired directions of two everyday text-editing keys into its entire subject.
summary: One line of text sits between two cursor marks. Each cursor removes one character at a time, advancing from its own side until the line is gone.
title: Which Way Is Delete?
